newsitem.title: TAIWAN: LAND BANK OF TAIWAN RAISES PRIME RATE TO 7.4 PCT.
newsitem.headline: LAND BANK OF TAIWAN RAISES PRIME RATE TO 7.4 PCT.

text.p: State-owned Land Bank of Taiwan on Thursday said it was raising its prime lending rate by 0.125 percentage point to 7.4 percent, effective Friday.
The bank also was raising its one-month-to-three-year time deposits rates by between 0.05 and 0.25 percentage point.
The Land Bank was the fourth state-owned financial institutions hiking the interest rates, following the step of the Bank of Taiwan, the island's biggest commercial bank, on Wednesday.
Various private commercial banks also raised rates.
The rate hikes came a week after the central bank's decision to increase two key interest rates to stabilise the foreign exchange market.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on July 31 the bank was raising the rediscount rate and accommodations against secured loans to 5.25 and 5.625 percent, respectively, effective August 1.
